matching_criterion_description: Presence of coloboma points toward alternative diagnoses such as CHARGE syndrome or complex chromosomal disorders, as coloboma was 0/12 (0%) in RAMELN cohorts.
Presence of microphthalmia argues strongly against RAMELN (0/12 assessed, 0%) and suggests alternative diagnoses like CHARGE syndrome.
Presence of infantile spasms eliminates non-syndromic primary microcephalies (e.g. ASPM, WDR62), though it is variable in RAMELN (53.8%).
Must be present in all affected individuals (100% penetrance) as part of the core neurodevelopmental triad.
Highly penetrant core feature (~84.6%) presenting in infancy.
High penetrance core feature presenting as congenital or postnatal deceleration of head circumference.
